title: What If Iceland's Katla Volcano Erupted Tomorrow?

scenes.text: What if Iceland's Katla volcano erupted tomorrow? The first danger isn't the ash.
Katla sits under an ice cap up to seven hundred meters thick, and it normally erupts every forty to eighty years.
The heat would melt ice fast. In 1918, the flood peaked near 300,000 cubic meters a second, and icebergs about thirty meters high were reported.
Then the ash. A large Katla eruption could throw out around six times the ash of the 2010 eruption that grounded European flights.
One volcanologist estimates the plume could climb twenty kilometers into the stratosphere, snarling flights for weeks.
Katla last erupted big in 1918, longer ago than its usual gap. When it wakes, the flood comes first.

description:
What if Iceland's Katla volcano erupted tomorrow?
It sits under a glacier, so the first danger is a giant flood, and the ash could be about six times 2010's flight-grounding cloud.
